slides.say: Given: diamond of three is equal to twenty-one. Which of the following cannot be the definition of the operation diamond?

This time they don't give us the rule. They only tell us one result. Someone took three, used the diamond, and got twenty-one. [short pause] We'll put three into the choices, one by one, until one of them doesn't give twenty-one.

[short pause] Many different rules could turn three into twenty-one. Seven x is one example, because seven times three is twenty-one. So a choice that gives twenty-one could be the rule, and we can't rule it out. We're looking for the one choice that does not give twenty-one.
Choice number one, x cubed minus six. Three cubed is twenty-seven, and twenty-seven minus six is twenty-one. It gives twenty-one, so it could be the rule. Choice number one is out.
Choice number two, x times, in brackets, x plus four. Three plus four is seven, and three times seven is twenty-one. It could be the rule too, so choice number two is out.
at: so choice number two is out

slides.say: Choice number three, five x plus five. Five times three is fifteen, and fifteen plus five is twenty. Twenty is not twenty-one. So this rule cannot turn three into twenty-one, and it cannot be the definition. Choice number three is our answer. That one failure is all the question asks for, so we can stop here without checking choice number four. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
